description.fun: A laid-back little croc whose flame sac is too small to hold its fire, so energy keeps leaking out of the dent on its head as flickering flames. It soaks up heat lounging on warm rocks, does everything at its own pace, and rushes at any food it spots. Like real crocodiles, it sometimes sleeps with one eye open.
description.guide: The Fire-type first partner Pokémon of Paldea, from Pokémon Scarlet and Violet. Fuecoco absorbs heat through its square scales and constantly leaks fire energy from its small flame sac. It evolves into Crocalor and then Skeledirge.
description.tagline: A carefree croc that leaks fire and loves its food

description.fun: Crocalor's fire energy and overflowing vitality have formed an egg-shaped fireball, sitting in a nest of flames on its head like a sombrero. The valve in its flame sac is tied to its vocal cords, so it lets out a guttural cry whenever it spews fire, and nobody would call that voice beautiful. Its skull-like markings seem to borrow from the calaveras of Mexico's Day of the Dead.
description.guide: The middle stage of Fuecoco's line. Crocalor carries an egg-shaped fireball in a nest of flame on its head and cries out as it breathes fire.
description.tagline: A croc with a fireball egg nesting on its head

description.fun: Skeledirge's gentle singing soothes the souls of all who hear it, while its flames, over 3,000 °C, burn its enemies to a crisp. The fiery bird on its head is a creature of its own: rumour says it was born when Crocalor's fireball gained a soul, and it turns into a microphone whenever Skeledirge sings. It's the heaviest of all the final first partner Pokémon.
description.guide: The final evolution of Fuecoco and Paldea's Fire-type first partner, a Fire and Ghost-type Pokémon themed on singers and the Day of the Dead. The bird on its head is a separate being said to have gained a soul.
description.tagline: A singing croc with a fiery bird for a microphone
